1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the revision, including the Annexures attached therewith.

2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 CrPC has been filed against the judgment and order dated 04.07.2008 passed by the Special Judge (Ayodhya Prakaran)/Additional Sessions Judge,
Lucknow in Criminal Appeal No.134 of 2005 preferred by the revisionist against the judgment and order dated 08.09.2005 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 25, Lucknow in Case No.1946 of 1987 registered under Section 7/16 The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'PFA Act,') at Police Station Nagram, District Lucknow.

Lucknow

sentences.text: 3. The trial Court, finding the revisionist guilty of the offence under Section 7/16 PFA Act, had convicted and sentenced him for one year imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in the event of non-payment of fine, three months additional imprisonment.

However, the learned appellate Court Shri Krishna vs State Of U.P. on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46481427/
1 modified the sentence to six months with fine of Rs.1,000/-.

entities.text: Krishna vs State Of U.P. on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4.The complainant, Food Inspector, on 24th October, 1985, at around 11.00 a.m., during the course of inspection, got suspicion that food item (Dalmoth) being sold by the revisionist was adulterated;
he bought 750 gram Dalmoth from the revisionist, and after preparing the samples, sent the samples for examination to the Public Analyst; the samples sent for examination was found to be wanting the parameters prescribed under the PFA Act.
5. Counsel for the revisionist states that the incident is of 1985; the revisionist had undergone 47 days imprisonment.

The learned counsel places reliance on judgment of the Supreme Court in Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, and states that after considering the age of the appellant, and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, the Supreme Court reduced the sentence to the period already undergone by the appellant in that case.

entities.text: Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the said judgment of the Supreme Court, and trivial nature of the offence committed by the revisionist, it would be appropriate to reduce the sentence to the sentence already undergone by the revisionist with enhanced fine.

7. In view thereof, the sentence awarded to the revisionist is reduced to the sentence already undergone by him with fine of Rs.2,000/- (Rupees two thousand) to be deposited by the revisionist with the trial Court within fifteen days from today.
8. Thus, the revision is allowed partly.

9. Let copy of this order, along with lower court record, if received, be sent to the concerned Court below forthwith for compliance.
[D.K. Singh, J.] Order Date :- 29.1.2020 MVS/-
